note: One skill = one pairing MEANING -> SENTENCE SHAPE. The order of this list is the order in which new skills are introduced. 'name' is the school name, shown only as a tooltip. Articles are left out on purpose: speech recognition silently repairs them, so spoken answers cannot be graded reliably.

skills.meaning: a situation that started in the past and is still true (how long so far)
skills.example: I've known her for ten years.
skills.name: present perfect (unfinished time)
skills.trap_pl: Po polsku czas teraźniejszy („znam ją od dziesięciu lat”), po angielsku have + past participle.

skills.meaning: a real possibility in the future and its result
skills.example: If the build fails, I'll roll it back.
skills.name: first conditional
skills.trap_pl: Po polsku „jeśli będę miał”, po angielsku po if nie ma will: if I have.

skills.meaning: a polite question wrapped inside another sentence
skills.pattern: Do you know / Could you tell me + question word + subject + verb
skills.example: Do you know where the meeting is?
skills.name: indirect question
skills.trap_pl: W środku nie ma szyku pytania: „where the meeting is”, nie „where is the meeting”.

skills.meaning: I want, expect or would like another person to do something
skills.pattern: want / would like / expect + person + to + verb
skills.example: I want you to check this before Friday.
skills.name: verb + object + to-infinitive
skills.trap_pl: Polskie „chcę, żebyś” to nie „I want that you”, tylko I want you to.

skills.meaning: a finished event at a stated time in the past
skills.example: I sent the invoice yesterday.
skills.name: past simple
skills.trap_pl: Gdy pada konkretny czas (yesterday, last week, in May), nie ma have: „I sent it yesterday”.

skills.meaning: the future after when, as soon as, until, before, after
skills.pl: przyszłość po when / as soon as
skills.pattern: will + verb ... when / as soon as / until + present simple
skills.example: I'll call you when I get there.
skills.name: future time clause
skills.trap_pl: Po polsku „kiedy dojadę / jak będę”, po angielsku po when nie ma will: when I get there.

skills.meaning: an unlikely or imaginary situation now and what would follow
skills.example: If I had more time, I'd rewrite it.
skills.name: second conditional
skills.trap_pl: Po if nie ma would: „if I had”, nie „if I would have”.

skills.meaning: something is necessary, not necessary, or forbidden
skills.pattern: have to + verb / don't have to + verb / mustn't + verb
skills.example: You don't have to come, it's optional.
skills.name: have to, don't have to, mustn't
skills.trap_pl: „Nie musisz” to don't have to. „Mustn't” znaczy „nie wolno”.

skills.meaning: something has just happened or is already done, and the result matters now
skills.pattern: have + (just / already) + past participle; haven't ... yet
skills.example: I've already sent the invoice.
skills.name: present perfect (result)

skills.meaning: after enjoy, avoid, keep, mind, suggest, finish, and after any preposition
skills.example: I'm looking forward to seeing you.
skills.name: gerund
skills.trap_pl: Po przyimku (to, about, of, without) zawsze -ing: looking forward to seeing, nie „to see”.

skills.meaning: asking who or what did something (the unknown is the doer)
skills.example: Who told you that?
skills.name: subject question
skills.trap_pl: Gdy pytasz o wykonawcę, nie ma did: „Who told you?”, nie „Who did tell you?”.

skills.meaning: a past that did not happen and its imagined result
skills.pattern: if + had + past participle, would have + past participle
skills.example: If I had asked earlier, I would have saved a week.
skills.name: third conditional

skills.meaning: an activity that started earlier and is still going on, or has just left a visible trace
skills.example: I've been working on this since Monday.
skills.name: present perfect continuous
skills.trap_pl: Po polsku „pracuję nad tym od poniedziałku”, po angielsku have been working.

skills.meaning: a good idea in the past that did not happen, or criticism of what was done
skills.pattern: should have / shouldn't have + past participle
skills.example: I should have backed it up first.
skills.name: should have + past participle

skills.meaning: a decision made right now, an offer or a promise
skills.example: Hang on, I'll send it right now.
skills.name: future simple (will)

skills.meaning: an intention I already have, or something I can see coming
skills.pattern: am / is / are going to + verb
skills.example: I'm going to look for a new job this year.
skills.name: be going to

skills.meaning: what happened to something, when the doer is unknown or unimportant
skills.example: The server was restarted last night.
skills.name: passive voice

skills.meaning: passing on what someone said earlier
skills.pattern: said / told me (that) + one step back in time
skills.example: She said she was busy all week.
skills.name: reported speech (statements)
skills.trap_pl: Po polsku czas zostaje („powiedziała, że jest zajęta”), po angielsku cofa się: she said she was busy.

skills.meaning: something that was true or regular in the past but is not any more
skills.example: I used to commute two hours a day.
skills.name: used to

skills.meaning: something in progress right now or temporary these days
skills.example: I'm working from home this week.
skills.name: present continuous

skills.meaning: what I do regularly, or a permanent fact
skills.example: I usually start at nine.
skills.name: present simple

skills.meaning: a guess about the present, with how sure I am
skills.example: She must be stuck in traffic.
skills.name: modals of deduction (present)

skills.meaning: saying which thing or person I mean, when a preposition is involved
skills.example: That's the client I told you about.
skills.name: relative clause with a stranded preposition
skills.trap_pl: Polskie „o którym ci mówiłem” to „I told you about”: przyimek idzie na koniec.

skills.meaning: I would like the present to be different
skills.example: I wish I had more time for this.
skills.name: wish + past

skills.meaning: someone else does it for me because I arranged it
skills.pl: zlecam, ktoś robi to za mnie
skills.example: I had my car serviced last week.
skills.name: causative have
skills.trap_pl: Po polsku „naprawiłem samochód” nawet u mechanika. Po angielsku wtedy „I had my car repaired”.

skills.meaning: life experience up to now, with no time given
skills.example: I've never worked in a startup.
skills.name: present perfect (experience)

skills.meaning: what was in progress when something else happened
skills.pattern: was / were + verb-ing ... when + past simple
skills.example: I was reviewing the code when the call came.
skills.name: past continuous

skills.meaning: passing on a question someone asked
skills.pattern: asked (me) + if / question word + subject + verb, one step back in time
skills.example: He asked me where I worked.
skills.name: reported question
skills.trap_pl: Bez szyku pytania i bez did: „he asked where I worked”.

skills.meaning: a guess about the past, with how sure I am
skills.pattern: must / might / can't + have + past participle
skills.example: He might have forgotten the meeting.
skills.name: modals of deduction (past)

skills.meaning: after decide, plan, manage, refuse, agree, offer, hope
skills.example: We decided to postpone the launch.
skills.name: to-infinitive

skills.meaning: the earlier of two past events
skills.example: The deadline had already passed when I noticed.
skills.name: past perfect

skills.meaning: something is no longer strange for me, or I am slowly adapting to it
skills.pattern: be / get used to + verb-ing or noun
skills.example: I'm used to working late.
skills.name: be / get used to
skills.trap_pl: To nie „used to work” (kiedyś pracowałem). Tu „to” jest przyimkiem, więc po nim -ing.

skills.meaning: how long something takes
skills.pattern: it takes (+ person) + time + to + verb
skills.example: It takes me an hour to get to the office.
skills.name: it takes ... to
skills.trap_pl: Polskie „dojazd zajmuje mi godzinę” zaczyna się po angielsku od it: it takes me an hour to get there.

skills.meaning: something that always happens under a condition
skills.example: If a meeting has no agenda, it runs long.
skills.name: zero conditional

skills.meaning: what I think or expect will happen
skills.example: I think it'll take about three months.
skills.name: will for predictions

skills.meaning: a fixed arrangement with other people in the near future
skills.pattern: am / is / are + verb-ing + future time
skills.example: I'm meeting the client on Thursday.
skills.name: present continuous for arrangements

skills.meaning: passing on a request, an order or advice
skills.example: She told me to wait outside.
skills.name: reported request
skills.trap_pl: Polskie „powiedziała, żebym poczekał” to „she told me to wait”, bez that.

skills.meaning: a regret about something in the past
skills.example: I wish I had said no at the start.
skills.name: wish + past perfect

skills.meaning: advice, or a warning about what is the wise thing to do
skills.example: You'd better check with legal first.
skills.name: should, had better

skills.meaning: saying which person or thing I mean
skills.example: The guy who hired me left a month later.
skills.name: defining relative clause

skills.meaning: what has been, will be, or must be done to something
skills.pattern: has been / will be / must be + past participle
skills.example: It has already been approved.
skills.name: passive with perfect and modal verbs

skills.meaning: a plan I had in the past that did not happen
skills.example: I was going to call you, but the day got away from me.
skills.name: future in the past
skills.trap_pl: Polskie „miałem zadzwonić” to „I was going to call”, nie „I had to call”.

skills.meaning: someone forces me to do something, or allows me to
skills.example: My boss let me leave early.
skills.name: make and let
skills.trap_pl: Po make i let nie ma to: „let me leave”, nie „let me to leave”.

skills.meaning: checking that I am right, or inviting agreement
skills.pattern: statement + opposite short question (isn't it? / haven't you? / did she?)
skills.example: You've met her before, haven't you?
skills.name: question tag

skills.meaning: a different past would change the present
skills.pattern: if + had + past participle, would + verb (now)
skills.example: If I had studied law, I'd be living in a different city now.
skills.name: mixed conditional

skills.meaning: I succeeded in doing something difficult on one occasion
skills.pattern: managed to + verb / was able to + verb
skills.example: I managed to fix it before the demo.
skills.name: managed to, was able to
skills.trap_pl: Jednorazowy sukces to „I managed to fix it”, nie „I could fix it”. Could opisuje ogólną umiejętność.

skills.meaning: how much or how many, and whether it is too much or not enough
skills.pattern: much / little + mass noun; many / few + plural; too much / not enough
skills.example: We don't have much time, and there are too many open issues.
skills.name: quantifiers

skills.meaning: two things are equal, or one does not reach the other
skills.pl: tak samo jak / nie tak jak
skills.example: The new version isn't as fast as the old one.
skills.name: as ... as

skills.meaning: something will be finished before a point in the future
skills.example: By Friday I'll have finished the migration.
skills.name: future perfect

skills.meaning: adding a comment about the whole thing I just said
skills.example: He was late again, which annoyed everyone.
skills.name: non-defining relative clause (sentential)
skills.trap_pl: Polskie „co” w komentarzu do całego zdania to which, nie what.

skills.meaning: with stop, remember, forget: looking back at an earlier action, or forward to the next one
skills.pattern: remember / stop + verb-ing (earlier action) vs + to + verb (next action)
skills.example: I remember locking the door. Remember to lock the door.
skills.name: verbs that change meaning with gerund or infinitive

skills.meaning: one thing changes together with another
skills.example: The longer we wait, the more it'll cost.
skills.name: double comparative

skills.meaning: stressing how strong something is and what it led to
skills.pattern: so + adjective (+ that) / such + (a) + adjective + noun (+ that)
skills.example: It was such a long meeting that I missed lunch.
skills.name: so and such

skills.meaning: what I would prefer, for myself or from someone else
skills.pattern: I'd rather + verb / I'd rather + person + past simple
skills.example: I'd rather you didn't mention it yet.
skills.name: would rather

skills.meaning: something that will be in progress at a specific future moment
skills.pl: o tej porze będę w trakcie
skills.example: This time next week I'll be sitting on a train.
skills.name: future continuous

skills.meaning: putting the spotlight on the one thing that matters
skills.example: What I need is one quiet hour.
skills.name: cleft sentence (what-cleft)
